full_judgment:
10. It is not disputed that the opposite party No.4(ka) is a necessary party and a proper party in the application for pre-emption and as such, the case is bad for defect of parties for non-joinder of a necessary party namely, opposite party No.4(Ka). 

 11. The learned Advocate for the respondents next submits that the point for consideration is whether such joinder of opposite party No.4(ka) after a lapse of 1-1/2 years from the date of institution of the pre-emption case shall make the pre-emption case itself barred by limitation as against the aforesaid added party. He further submits that section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that the procedure provided in the Code in regard to suits shall be followed, as far as it can be made applicable, in all proceedings in any court of civil jurisdiction. He further submits that an application for pre-emption under section 96 of the Act is governed by the provisions of The Code of Civil Procedure. He also submits that sub-rule (5) of rule 10 of Order 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that subject to the provisions of section 22 of the Limitation Act, the proceedings as against any person added as opposite party shall be deemed to have begun only on the service of the summons/notice upon him. Section 22 of the Limitation Act provides that where after the institution of the suit if a new defendant is added, the suit shall, as regards him, be deemed to have been instituted when he was not made a party, provided that such addition has not been made owing to an assignment or devolution of any interest during the pendency of the suit. The learned Advocate for the respondents further submits that since the opposite party No. 4(ka) was added after a lapse of 1-1/2 years from the institution of the case under section. 96 of the Act, the case is hopelessly barred by limitation and must fail on this count alone. In support of his contention he has relied upon the case of Girl Bala Das vs. Vasudev Dey and others, reported in 32 DLR 68. In that case it was held: 

 15. Mr. MA Rahim cited the case reported in 42 DLR (AD) 110 and submits that if an amendment is allowed it will relate back to the date of the institution of the pre-emption. This amendment refers to an amendment under Order 6 rule 14 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But in the instant case there was no such amendment. On the other hand, there was addition of party under Order 1 rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the instant case the appellants have been able to show that a valuable legal right had accrued in their favour for not impleading opposite party no.4(Ka) within the statutory period of limitation. For not impleading the opposite party No. 4 (Ka) within time, the pre-emption application has become time-barred. In the case reported in 42 DLR (AD) 110 it was held that as a rule no amendment is allowed where its effect will take away any legal right which might have accrued by lapse of time. In the instant case, as I have already pointed out that a valuable legal right has already accrued in favour of the opposite parties for non-impleading opposite party No.4(Ka) within time.
